explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/21: f(n) is minimal such that an intersecting family of n-sets with |F| = f(n) has every S with |S| ≤ n−1 disjoint from some member; is f(n) ≪ n? `IsErdosLovaszFamily` encodes this over the ground set ℕ, which loses no generality for finite families, and `f` is the sInf of sizes. Families exist for n ≥ 1 (all n-subsets of a (2n−1)-set), so sInf is not junk there; only n = 0 is degenerate. The statement is ∃ C, ∀ᶠ n, f n ≤ C·n. The page records this as solved by Kahn. Faithful.
